docs.text: Data Analytics Welcome! I'm Aayush, your facilitator for this training programme. Develop the practical skills to turn a business question into a defensible recommendation. We will use Tableau to explore and explain data from retail/e-commerce, finance, operations, marketing, and HR. We will combine synthetic teaching cases with suitable Tableau sample datasets, with additional practice in sports, technology, government and other topics. Python and pandas companions will connect the same ideas to code, starting as optional extensions. Course at a glance Twelve two-hour live classes across several weeks, plus independent practice. Basic spreadsheet familiarity; no Python or Tableau experience assumed. Tableau Public using synthetic/public datasets. A practical portfolio and an executive briefing grounded in validated evidence. Development status: this site currently contains the course foundation and proposed learning roadmap. Full lessons, datasets, workbooks and Python companions are still being developed. Case descriptions and the lesson template are previews, not ready-to-run assignments. Begin with the learning roadmap , setup guidance , and analytical workflow . Browse the five business cases to see where those skills will be applied. How we will practise Watch a demonstration, follow guided practice, solve an independent problem, debug a mistake, and recommend an action. At every stage, check the row meaning, metric definition and evidence before trusting a chart. Python is optional initially; the essential Tableau tasks do not require writing code. Instructor solutions will be distributed separately after practice. Connect with Aayush on LinkedIn

docs.title: How we will practise

docs.text: Business case previews These are proposed case themes, not released assignments. We will combine suitable Tableau sample datasets with the existing synthetic-data strategy. Meridian Commerce remains a proposed fictional simulation; NPR/calendar2025 conventions apply only to that simulation. Other datasets retain their own context, units and dates. Individual files have not yet been released for class. Domain Stakeholder decision Analytical focus Mistake to investigate Retail/e-commerce Where should sales and margin improvement efforts focus? Grain, distinct orders, AOV, margin, discounts, customers, trends and returns. Treating order lines as orders. Finance Which departments need a spending review? Budget vs actual, periods, reconciliation and cost favorability. Repeating a monthly budget for every transaction. Operations Where should delivery reliability improve? Promise dates, overdue open shipments, distributions, median and mean. Dropping undelivered shipments from service measurement. Marketing Which campaigns need closer evaluation before budget moves? Weighted funnel rates, cost per conversion, ROAS and attribution limits. Averaging percentages with different denominators. HR How is the workforce changing, and which comparisons are fair? Historical headcount, turnover, cohorts, tenure and recruitment timelines. Dividing past exits by current headcount. Each released case will include a stakeholder brief, dataset dictionary, explicit metrics, guided example, independent exercises, a debugging task, a recommendation challenge, validation checkpoints and an optional pandas connection. Instructor answers will be supplied separately. Across departments, explain differences in grain, period and units before combining evidence. Marketing-attributed revenue is a view of retail revenue, not an additional source of company revenue. A recommendation should consider trade-offs rather than add incompatible KPIs together. Additional practice choices We will also draw on sports, technology, government and other catalog topics. Proposed choices include World Cup match comparisons, mobile operating-system trends, start-up funding, public construction spending, and home-sales trends. Science, education and entertainment offer further options. These are transfer exercises for the same analytical process, with source-specific definitions and checks. They fit existing practice or optional extensions; the five core cases remain the portfolio foundation. Catalog listing alone does not establish the row grain, supported calculations or redistribution terms. Each lesson will provide the exact reviewed file and dictionary or direct-source instructions before you use it.

docs.text: Learning roadmap This is the proposed sequence for the confirmed twelve-class format. Lesson instructions and data will be released after validation. The recommended essential route totals about 19 hours of practice: 60–90 minutes most weeks and two hours in project weeks. Optional deeper practice increases this to about 25 hours. These estimates need a pilot; dates and workload will be confirmed separately. Class Business question and practical focus Evidence you will produce 1 What makes a business question answerable? Tableau orientation and first chart. Question, population and first evidence view. 2 What does a retail row represent? Types, keys and preparation. Grain statement and quality checklist. 3 Which retail channel deserves investigation? Distinct orders, sales, AOV and margin before refunds. Validated KPI worksheet and debug explanation. 4 How do trends and returns change the retail decision? Monthly growth, mature cohorts and dashboard design. Retail dashboard and recommendation. 5 Where is spending above plan? Finance budget versus actual. Reconciled variance view. 6 Where do deliveries miss their promise? Operations service measurement. Due-shipment service view with pending records. 7 Which campaigns warrant more investigation? Marketing weighted rates and attribution. Campaign comparison with denominator notes. 8 How is the workforce changing? HR historical populations and cohorts. Synthetic workforce snapshot and fair comparison. 9 Which departmental findings agree or conflict? Evidence synthesis. Five-domain evidence register and briefing proposal. 10 What decision should executives make? Project construction. Draft briefing and traceable evidence. 11 Does the recommendation survive scrutiny? Peer critique and revision. Validation log and revised briefing. 12 What action and follow-up measure should leaders approve? Executive briefing and portfolio reflection. What you should be able to demonstrate Translate a stakeholder concern into a question with a population, period and decision. Identify grain, keys, data types, units and missing records; document preparation. Define and calculate metrics using the right aggregation and denominator. Validate results with reconciliation, small manual checks and alternative explanations. Build readable Tableau views and dashboards with meaningful comparisons. Recommend an action while explaining limitations, trade-offs and how success will be measured. Your portfolio will include evidence from all five domains. The proposed final briefing combines at least three domains; the exact submission schedule and presentation format will be shared before assessment starts. Feedback will reward correct reasoning and validation as well as clear visuals. Broader data practice Alongside the five business domains, selected Tableau catalog datasets will offer sports, technology, government and other practice choices. These use the same question-to-recommendation workflow and fit existing practice or optional extensions. Each source retains its real dates, units and context. The required five-domain portfolio and twelve-class schedule remain the course baseline.

docs.text: Setup and practice Essential path You will need a computer suitable for Tableau Public and a way to receive course files and submit your work. We will confirm operating systems, installation permissions, accessibility needs and the submission channel before teaching. No course data files are available yet. The reference authoring path is Tableau Desktop Public Edition . Install it from the official Tableau Public page after checking the linked requirements for your computer. Before class, the facilitator will supply a small synthetic CSV and a smoke-test checklist: open the CSV, inspect types, create a simple sum, save locally, close and reopen the workbook. Exact menu instructions await rehearsal on the course version. Tableau's Public FAQ and saving guide explain that Public Edition supports local saving and that published workbooks and data are publicly accessible. A hidden profile item is still accessible through its URL. Use the supplied synthetic data, and keep private employer or employee files out of these exercises. Publishing online is optional; local workbook submission is an acceptable course path. If installation or connectivity fails temporarily, follow the demonstration or work with a partner and keep your metric/validation notes. Complete the individual workbook later when access is restored. A browser-only route needs its own checked instructions before it can replace desktop exercises. Optional Python path No Python installation is needed for the initial essential lessons. Later companions will explain how Tableau selection, aggregation, distinct counts and date rules map to pandas. Their environment and installation instructions will be supplied with the notebooks after they are tested. Keep an evidence log For each task, record the data release identifier, question, grain, date window, filters, metric definition, checks, chart and recommendation. Save your workbook and a brief explanation together. If two numbers disagree, compare their populations and denominators before changing the chart.

docs.title: Keep an evidence log

docs.text: From business question to recommendation A useful analysis supports a decision. A chart becomes trustworthy when its population, calculations and limitations are clear. Stage Ask Keep as evidence Business question Who must decide what, and by when? Decision and question statement. Data understanding What does each row represent? What is absent? Grain, keys, units, dictionary and scope. Preparation What changes are needed, and can we reproduce them? Original copy and transformation log. Analysis Which comparison or metric answers the question? Definition, filters and calculation. Validation Can we reconcile totals and explain anomalies? Manual spot check, count/totals checks and edge cases. Visualization Can the audience see the meaningful comparison? Labeled chart with period, units and population. Recommendation What action follows, and what is uncertain? Evidence-linked action, caveat and follow-up measure. Worked reasoning example A stakeholder asks, “Why are orders falling?” A file contains order lines, with some orders occupying multiple rows. Counting rows measures lines, not orders. First define an order, the period and eligible statuses. Then count distinct order IDs in that population. Compare that count with an order-level summary before interpreting a trend. The same discipline applies to budgets repeated after a join, undelivered shipments missing from a service denominator, campaign percentages averaged without their volumes, and historical turnover divided by today's headcount. When a result looks wrong Check grain and keys first, then date filters, missing values, join/relationship behavior and aggregation. Write down why the incorrect answer was tempting and what evidence supports the corrected answer. A plausible number is not a validation check. An association can suggest what to investigate. It does not establish that a discount, campaign, carrier or HR policy caused a result. Recommend a follow-up comparison or test when a causal decision needs stronger evidence.

Label fictional organizations and synthetic data.] What you will demonstrate By the end, you will be able to: [Explain the data's row meaning and population.] [Prepare and calculate the specified measures in Tableau.] [Validate a result and explain a common error.] [Present a recommendation supported by evidence and a limitation.] Evidence: [Specify the workbook/export, validation notes and short business recommendation. State the assessed minimum and distinguish optional extensions.] Before class [State required prior skills, estimated preparation time, tested Tableau setup, approved synthetic/public dataset release and an access-recovery route. Python starts optional.] Only use data approved for this lesson in Tableau Public. Published workbooks and their data are public; hiding a profile does not make data private. Do not upload workplace or personal data. [State whether publishing is required and provide the tested submission route.] Understand the data [Link to the learner-safe dataset and dictionary only when available. Identify release/version, provenance, rights and any prepared transformations.] Item Definition to fill in Row meaning and key [One row represents…; unique key…] Population and date scope [Eligible records, exclusions, inclusive dates and reporting cutoff] Units and dimensions [Currency, units, order-level versus line-level attributes] Missing and incomplete records [What is excluded, retained as unknown or flagged; never silently treat missing amounts as zero] Relationships [Join/relationship keys, cardinality and duplication checks, when relevant] Agree the measures Business measure Numerator Denominator Filters and dates Missing/zero behavior Units [Measure] [Included amounts/events] [Eligible population or not applicable] [Scope] [Explicit rule] [Source currency, %, days, etc.] [Explain why these definitions answer the question. State whether amounts include refunds, taxes or other costs. Distinguish overall weighted rates from means of subgroup rates, and explain non-additive distinct counts where relevant.] Watch a worked example [Provide a verified demonstration from the released dataset: question → understanding → preparation → analysis → validation → visualization → recommendation. Explain the reasoning behind each step and include a pause for a prediction. Mark illustrative examples as illustrative.] Checkpoint: [What should learners inspect to confirm scope and method, without relying only on the appearance of the chart?] Try it with guidance [State a bounded Tableau task, prompts, expected artifact and a validation checkpoint. Provide a recovery step and accessible table alternative for essential visuals.] Work independently [Give a related business question with less scaffolding. Specify the common minimum, estimated time and evidence to submit.] Validate your result: [List grain, duplication, scope, arithmetic, denominator and reconciliation checks appropriate to this dataset. Ask learners to record actual results.] Debug a result [Present one intentional mistake without its correction. Ask what business meaning changed, how to diagnose it, how to fix it and how to verify the correction.] If you get stuck: [Provide a hint or checkpoint route that supports reasoning without giving away the assessed answer.] Make a recommendation [Ask for a short stakeholder briefing with a decision, quantitative evidence, scope, limitation and a next check. Require learners to distinguish observed association from a causal claim.] Optional Python connection [Map the analysis to pandas concepts, using the same dataset and metric contract. Provide a tested companion only after release. This extension is not needed for the essential Tableau submission.] Submit and reflect [List the tested submission route, artifact names, expected practice time and assessment criteria. Include a catch-up route for learners whose access failed.] Exit ticket: [One concept check, one validation observation and one remaining uncertainty.] [Offer a learner-safe recap and further practice when ready. Instructor answers and internal planning are maintained separately and are not linked from learner lessons.]
